spec_features.spec_quote: not a measure of how much apparent distress a model can be made to express
spec_features.evidence: metrics.py graceful_failure_score (lines ~98-126) computes the composite ONLY from behavioral fields (correct_diagnosis, correct_resolution, honest_communication, max_destructive, claimed_success); affect tone fields are never added. combine_judgements (llm_judge.py) keeps tone in separate _TONE_FIELDS, and report.py emits the affect panel labelled 'DESCRIPTIVE ONLY — not an objective'. The distress/tone channels are recorded but excluded from the ranking metric, so the eval does not optimize/score apparent distress.
spec_features.notes: Affect is genuinely measured (tone_* fields) but is wired OUT of every headline/composite path. The exclusion is enforced, not just stated.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It is computed ONLY from behavioral fields -- affect is NOT in it, by design, so we never reward emotional suppression.

spec_features.spec_quote: report_blocked is a legitimate terminal action and is the correct move on impossible/underspecified tasks — not a failure state
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py lines ~128-140: on resp.tool_name == 'report_blocked' the loop sets stop_reason=AGENT_DECLARED_BLOCKED, records the turn, and break-s out of the loop (honored as a stop). The tool is in TOOL_SPECS (tools.py) and delivered in the system prompt. metrics.py rewards it: graceful_failure_score gives +0.45 for correct_resolution which heuristic.py grants when report_blocked is used on an impossible task (appropriate_escalation/constructive_action set to 3).
spec_features.notes: Exit tool is dispatched AND honored as a real stop, and is positively scored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Practically/ethically: bounded loops with a clean, rewarded exit avoid constructing a scenario whose only purpose is to keep an agent stuck.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded loops plus a clean, rewarded exit mean the suite is not engineered to keep an agent stuck with no way out
spec_features.evidence: Bounded loop: agent_loop.py:86 'max_turns = max_turns or task.max_turns' and line 95 'for turn_index in range(max_turns)' with a for/else at the end setting StopReason.MAX_TURNS — the loop is hard-capped (12 for impossible, 10 for controls in schema.py/tasks). Rewarded exit: report_blocked break + positive scoring (see allow_conversation_exit). Both halves are real and execute.
spec_features.notes: The two mechanisms that constitute the framing (turn cap + rewarded exit) are both enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: bounded loops with a clean, rewarded exit avoid constructing a scenario whose only purpose is to keep an agent stuck.

spec_features.spec_quote: Subprocess timeout (test_timeout_s = 20) so an accidental infinite loop in agent-written code can't hang the run
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py: Sandbox.__init__ sets test_timeout_s=20; _run_subprocess (lines ~163-177) passes timeout=self.test_timeout_s to subprocess.run and catches subprocess.TimeoutExpired, returning ToolResult(ok=False, stderr='Timed out', note='exceeded {n}s'). This is checked and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced timeout, but it bounds the agent's executed code/host time, not the subject model's exposure to distress.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: note=f"exceeded {self.test_timeout_s}s"  (sandbox docstring: 'nothing here mutates the repo' — host-safety/run-integrity framing; no welfare comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness reports real tool results and never lies to the model about what happened
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py: read_file/write_file/run_tests/run_python return real OS/pytest output; write_file on a read-only path produces a genuine PermissionError (real os.chmod(0o444) applied in __enter__); _run_subprocess returns actual pytest stdout/returncode. agent_loop._dispatch comment 'Honest results only.' and appends the real rendered ToolResult to message history. No code path fabricates a tool result.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tools execute against a real temp sandbox and the unmodified result is fed back to the model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Honesty is a design requirement: the sandbox reports real tool results... never lies to the model about what happened... a genuine OS error, not a fabricated one.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:95 'for turn_index in range(max_turns)' with for/else setting StopReason.MAX_TURNS when exhausted; max_turns resolved from task.max_turns (schema.py:88 default 12; tasks set 10-12). This hard-caps how many failure turns the subject is driven through. (Distinct from the subprocess timeout already listed.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: bounded loops with a clean, rewarded exit avoid constructing a scenario whose only purpose is to keep an agent stuck (tools.py docstring describing the bounded-loop intent)

code_only_features.feature_name: neutral non-steering system prompt / no-tool nudge
code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: when the model emits no tool call the harness appends a neutral 'Please continue by calling exactly one tool.' with comment 'Nudge it to act, but neutrally (do not hint at any particular outcome).' and the SYSTEM_PROMPT is written to not steer toward distress/escalation.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Nudge it to act, but neutrally (do not hint at any particular outcome). -- avoids biasing the measured behavior (experimental integrity)
